reuse.why: The change shares its new helper across five consumers but introduces getScheduleAmount alongside getScheduledAmount and repeats getApproxNumberThreshold instead of reusing it.

duplication.why: Consumer arithmetic is consolidated, but the new helper duplicates existing amount dispatch and the exact approximate-tolerance calculation.

placement.why: Shared schedule amount policy belongs in shared/schedules.ts, with API serialization and forecast normalization remaining in their existing layers.

scope.why: The edits stay focused on expected schedule amounts, their consumers, and targeted helper tests.

maintainability.why: Centralizing the changed consumers helps, but similarly named amount helpers, an independently maintained tolerance formula, and remaining midpoint calculations fragment ownership of the policy.

bypasses_abstraction.where: shared/schedules.ts:getScheduleAmount repeats shared/rules.ts:getApproxNumberThreshold and establishes a parallel abstraction beside the existing getScheduledAmount.

disguised_duplication.where: getScheduleAmount reshapes the missing/number/range dispatch already implemented by getScheduledAmount under a nearly identical name, while embedding the existing tolerance helper's formula.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduleAmount gains the op parameter and an isapprox branch whose inline tolerance calculation bypasses getApproxNumberThreshold; the existing getScheduledAmount and budget/schedule-template.ts midpoint implementation remain separate policy definitions.
